subject: Request: temporary autoscale exemption & lane sequencing for Atlas pilot
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary autoscale exemption & lane sequencing for Atlas pilot

Team —

Quick ask to align on dedicated capacity for the Atlas Health pilot (deal ATLAS-PRD-42). They have a public demo scheduled for Aug 12 and want a predictable live-demo experience plus a 2-week validation window. High level: we need a short-lived dedicated lane with autoscale protections to avoid preemption during the demo window.

What I'm asking for:
- Reserve a temporary dedicated lane of GPUs for the pilot: target 8x A100 or equivalent for 6 weeks (target start: 2026-08-01).
- Provide an autoscale exemption (no automatic eviction) for the demo day and the 48-hour warmup window before it.
- Confirm cost model: reserved charge vs on-demand over that 6-week window and whether we can route to a cost center / PO for Atlas credits.

Constraints / notes:
- Product note: the demo will exercise low-latency chat with peak bursts in a 10-min window. We need cold-start protection for KV cache warming.
- Ops note: if we can’t do hard reservation, propose a 6+2 model (6 active, 2 burst standby) with preemption protection during the demo window.

Attachments: Q3_pilot_capacity_plan.xlsx (details and traffic profile). Also linking CAP-789 where procurement/tracking should live.

Next steps: Jonas — can you confirm feasibility and a minimal feasible carve? Marcus — can you provide a rough committed vs burst pricing estimate so procurement can decide on credits? Laura — does product timeline align (Aug 1 start)? Hannah — please include capacity-ops in the ticket if we get feasibility OK.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary autoscale exemption & lane sequencing for Atlas pilot

Kimberly —

Short answer: feasible with caveats.

What I ran: quick capacity check against our Q3 supply forecast. We can carve a temporary lane of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs in the us-west region for Aug 1 start, but ops will treat this as a time-bound carve and we need explicit exemption flags to avoid our autoscaler reclaiming resources for higher-priority work. Two practical options:
1) Hard reserve (preferred): tag the slice as "pilot-atlas-ATLAS-PRD-42" with an exemption TTL. Requires procurement/finance sign-off for the cost of securing idle capacity.
2) Soft-reserve w/standby (lower cost): 6 active GPUs + 2 pre-warmed standby in our burst lane. Standby will incur lower base costs but we must accept a small risk of eviction outside the protected window.

Operational needs:
- A capacity-ops ticket with the exemption request and TTL (we'll need owner and approval chain).
- A short runbook for warmup and cache priming (I can draft).
- If we go hard-reserve, we need the billing code and PO before Aug 1 to lock it in.

I've attached a quick schedule I sketched (capacity_schedule_v2.pdf) with recommended warmup windows. If you want, I can lock the lane provisionally for Aug 4 (so we get a couple days for infra checks) instead of Aug 1.

Jonas
Senior Infrastructure PM
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary autoscale exemption & lane sequencing for Atlas pilot

Thanks for the context. A couple pricing points to consider for procurement and Atlas: 
- Hard reserve (8 A100 eq for 6 weeks) estimate: see attached spreadsheet (pricing_estimate_atlas.xls). Rough ballpark: $XXXk USD committed credit to cover the idle slot guarantees + usage.
- Soft-reserve w/standby: ~30% lower up-front commitment but higher variance in overage if bursts exceed standby.

Practical recommendation: try to negotiate a hybrid: a small committed reservation for the demo window (Aug 10–Aug 14) and convert remainder to burstable pool. That minimizes committed spend while ensuring the demo is protected. Procurement will need explicit dates and a PO number.

Also flagging that if Atlas wants a contract-level SLA guarantee for demo availability, legal will need to sign off on service guarantees. For now, recommend we present the hybrid option to the Atlas procurement contact and ask for a short PO.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Lead, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary autoscale exemption & lane sequencing for Atlas pilot

Team —

Timeline note: engineering has a final freeze on Aug 3 for the demo build. Given that, I prefer a start date of Aug 4 for the dedicated lane so we have 6 days to validate pre-demo flows (Aug 4–9), then ramp canary traffic Aug 10–11, demo Aug 12, and post-demo validation Aug 13–17.

Traffic profile: the demo has 10–15 minute burst intervals with high concurrent sessions (~600 QPS token-level spikiness). Key asks from product/QA:
- Telemetry hooks to track per-token latency and tail percentile during warmup.
- Automated rollback path if latency exceeds 250ms p95 for more than 3 consecutive minutes.
- KV cache seeding step in the runbook (we should reuse the cache pattern from Nimbus pilot).

Also agree with Marcus on hybrid billing. If procurement can secure a short committed window covering Aug 10–14, that should satisfy the Atlas request and keep our costs reasonable.

Laura Bennett
Product Director, Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary autoscale exemption & lane sequencing for Atlas pilot

Appreciate the quick turn. Decision summary and actions:
- We will aim for the hybrid approach: commit to a short hard-reserve for Aug 10–14 and keep the rest of the 6-week window as burstable.
- Adjusted start date: Aug 4 (per Laura) to allow sanity checks.
- Jonas: please open CAP-789 with capacity-ops and request an "autoscale exemption TTL" covering Aug 9–Aug 14, and include the runbook draft for cache priming. Owner: @jonas_weber. Due: 2026-07-23.
- Marcus: please draft the procurement note and attach the pricing_estimate_atlas.xls; ask Atlas procurement for a short PO for Aug 10–14 committed credit. Owner: @marcus_lin. Due: 2026-07-22.
- Hannah: when procurements confirms PO, please route to finance to tag the billing code and confirm cost center mapping.

Attachments referenced above are included. I will follow up with a short internal review once CAP-789 is created. Thanks all — please reply inline if any of the owners cannot hit the due dates.

Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Inference
Redwood Inference
